function: Channel estimation of the cascaded BS-RIS-user channel, with compression and denoising, in semi-passive RIS-assisted multiuser gMIMO (pp. 11-13).
system: Multiuser gMIMO with 1024 BS antennas; semi-passive reflecting RIS with active and passive elements, 24 x 24 UPA; 2.4 GHz carrier, 25 MHz subchannel (pp. 5, 17).
method: Quantized deep learning (qDL): encoder-decoder with stacked denoising MLP units, loss compensation and feedforward training modules; supervised regression trained with MSE loss (pp. 12-13, 17).
data_channel: Own model: Friis path loss (near and far field) with Rician fading, ratio unity; 110,000 samples for training and validation, source not stated (pp. 9-11, 17).
test_conditions: Random training and testing split of one dataset (p. 8); SINR swept up to 60 dB; gMIMO, mMIMO, MIMO and 12x12, 24x24 RIS shown as training curves (pp. 18-20).
baselines: Classical: none. Learned: LSTM [101], CSDL [10] (compressive sensing with deep learning), CNN [104], RNN [106] (pp. 17-18).
metrics: NMSE versus SINR and training steps, CDF of NMSE, and accuracy versus SINR and training steps (pp. 17-20).
q1_support: p. 9: "an RIS communication channel is modeled by including a combined radiation field, an RF chain matrix, and a qDL metric". Own model with Friis path loss (p. 9) and Rician fading (p. 11); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 17: "we set the total number of samples to 110,000 for training and validation". Only SINR sweeps (p. 18) and per-configuration curves versus training steps (Figs. 8, 11); no cross-condition test. Transfer learning is only a general option (p. 9), never reported.
q3_support: p. 17: "Figure 6 shows the NMSE as a function of the SINR for the proposed qDL, LSTM, CSDL, CNN, and RNN schemes." All baselines are learned; no non-learned method (LS, MMSE, OMP) is compared.
q4_support: p. 13: "As the model shrinks, the computational and memory requirements also decrease, resulting in lower latencies." Qualitative only; no order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime. The power term P_qDL (p. 22) is an energy model.
q5_support: p. 17: "we set the total number of samples to 110,000 for training and validation". The data source is not stated; no link or DOI to code or data, and no public dataset is named.
notes: Title on page 1 matches the DOI. Area 2: the learned qDL estimator recovers the cascaded channel (NMSE). The closed-form SINR, energy efficiency and reflection-coefficient analysis (pp. 14-16, 21-24) is not learned. The qDL channel model of Section IV is the authors' own signal model, not a learned generator. Stacked metasurfaces are only mentioned on p. 2. Network sizes are not reported.
